name: Grad Coach
shortDescription: Dissertation and thesis supervision turned into video — the structural mistakes that cost students months, from a service that has seen thousands of them.
longDescription: A dissertation coaching business publishing what it has learned across a stated ten thousand-plus projects. {{longCountWords|cap}} of the {{scannedWords}} most recent uploads pass twenty minutes and those are the substantial ones — thirty-six to thirty-nine minute sessions on the lessons that recur, the questions students actually ask, and the things supervisors wish were understood before the first chapter is written. The median is {{medianPhrase}}, so most of the catalogue is short single-topic answers. What distinguishes it from the other creator here is scope: this is about the shape of a long research project — scoping a question so it can be finished, structuring a literature review, knowing when methodology is settled enough to write — rather than about the sentence-level craft of academic prose.
notFor: Anyone outside a formal degree programme. Everything assumes a supervisor, a submission deadline and an institution's requirements, and none of it is about writing better sentences.

categories.why: The project rather than the prose — scoping, structure and sequencing across a whole dissertation, which is where the months are actually lost.
categories.evidence: 37 minutes on the lessons that save students months, 39 on what supervisors wish were understood earlier, 36 answering the questions that recur, and 36 drawing on a stated ten thousand-plus dissertations.

entryVideo.title: INSIDER Dissertation Advice: 5 Lessons That Can Save You MONTHS of Stress
entryVideo.whyThisOne: The failure modes stated up front, which is the one thing worth knowing before you start rather than after — and it shows the register before you commit to the archive.

caveats: This is a coaching service's channel and the free videos are its shop window; the ten thousand figure is the company's own and we have not verified it. Nobody is named as the teacher across the catalogue.

name: Rob Berger
jurisdictionNote: US account structures throughout — 401(k), IRA, Social Security timing and US tax treatment. The stress-testing method and the questions he asks of a plan transfer anywhere; the accounts, the rules and the numbers do not.
shortDescription: Retirement plans taken apart on screen — running a real withdrawal strategy until it breaks, and saying which part broke.
longDescription: The useful material is a run of twenty-minute-plus pieces that do something most retirement content avoids: take a specific plan and stress it. A twenty-five-year withdrawal strategy modelled until it fails, with the failure point named. The three kinds of guaranteed retirement income and why almost nobody ends up with all three. A real sixteen-fund portfolio graded holding by holding. There is also a full recorded course on a planning tool, over two hours. The median is {{medianPhrase}} and {{shortCountWords}} of the {{scannedWords}} most recent uploads are under two minutes, so the channel reads as a shorts feed at a glance and the substance has to be sought out.
notFor: Anyone outside the United States looking for what to do rather than how to think — the account types are US-specific and the tax treatment more so. Also not for someone at the start of their working life; the framing is people approaching or in retirement.

categories.why: The US half of a category that had only a UK voice — and the blurb turns on which account structures to use, which is the most jurisdiction-bound thing in personal finance.
categories.evidence: 19 minutes stress-testing a 25-year withdrawal plan to its breaking point, 22 on the three kinds of guaranteed retirement income, 23 grading a real 16-fund portfolio, and a 144-minute recorded course on retirement modelling.

entryVideo.title: I Stress-Tested a Real 25-Year Withdrawal Plan. Here's Where It Broke
entryVideo.whyThisOne: A plan run until it fails, with the failure named — which teaches more about what a retirement plan has to survive than any amount of advice about saving more.

caveats: He sells courses and tool subscriptions and the long recorded course is one of them. Most of the catalogue by count is short-form; the analysis is in a small number of long videos.
